section_summary: This section comprises U.S. State Department records relating to Japanese radio broadcasting and wireless communication from August 1931 to September 1938. It is centered around an exhaustive 1931 consular report detailing the legal regulation, government control, programming, receiver distribution, and technical infrastructure of radio in Japan under the Nippon Hoso Kyokai. Subsequent correspondence and cross-reference records address radio-press relations, mutual Sino-Japanese short-wave radio propaganda following the outbreak of fighting in 1937, and Japanese short-wave goodwill broadcasts directed to Brazil in 1938.

subfiles.about: Comprehensive voluntary consular report surveying the status, administration, legislation, educational use, and technical development of radio broadcasting in Japan.
subfiles.from: Hiram Bingham, Jr., American Vice Consul, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive report surveys the rapid growth and strict government regulation of radio broadcasting in Japan under the monopoly of the Nippon Hoso Kyokai. It details administrative oversight and censorship by the Department of Communications, operational statistics and programming schedules across twelve operating stations, and listener demographics. Appended are translations of Japanese broadcasting ordinances and the Wireless Telegraph Law, a station map, and captioned photographs illustrating broadcasting facilities and activities.
